en: I taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvan, the sun; Vivasvan taught it to Manu, and Manu passed it on to Ikshvaku.
speaker: Krishna said

sa: स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप ॥
tr: sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa
en: Handed down in this way, one to the next, the royal sages knew it. But over a long stretch of time, scorcher of foes, this yoga was lost to the world.

sa: स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः।
भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥
tr: sa evāyaṃ mayā te'dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ
bhakto'si me sakhā ceti rahasyaṃ hyetaduttamam
en: That same ancient yoga I have taught you today, because you are my devotee and my friend. This is the supreme secret.

sa: अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः।
tr: aparaṃ bhavato janma paraṃ janma vivasvataḥ
en: Your birth came later and Vivasvan's long before. How am I to understand that you taught it in the beginning?
speaker: Arjuna said

sa: बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन।
तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप ॥
tr: bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna
tānyahaṃ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha parantapa
en: Many births of mine have passed, and of yours too, Arjuna. I know them all; you do not, scorcher of foes.
speaker: Krishna said

en: Though I am unborn and my Self does not perish, though I am lord of all beings, I take charge of my own nature and come into being through my own power.

sa: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।
tr: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata
en: Whenever dharma declines and adharma rises, Bharata, I bring myself forth.
To protect the good, to destroy those who do evil, and to set dharma firmly in place, I come into being age after age.

sa: जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः।
त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन ॥
tr: janma karma ca me divyamevaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ
tyaktvā dehaṃ punarjanma naiti māmeti so'rjuna
en: Whoever truly knows my divine birth and work, Arjuna, is not born again on leaving the body, but comes to me.
Free from attachment, fear and anger, absorbed in me and taking refuge in me, many, purified by the discipline of knowledge, have reached my state.

sa: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम्।
tr: ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃstathaiva bhajāmyaham
en: However people come to me, so I receive them. All people follow my path, Partha, in every way.

sa: काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः।
क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा ॥
tr: kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiṃ yajanta iha devatāḥ
kṣipraṃ hi mānuṣe loke siddhirbhavati karmajā
en: Wanting success in their work, people here worship the gods, for in the human world success born of action comes quickly.
I created the four orders according to the division of qualities and work. Though I am their maker, know me as the non-doer, unchanging.

sa: न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा।
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते ॥
tr: na māṃ karmāṇi limpanti na me karmaphale spṛhā
iti māṃ yo'bhijānāti karmabhirna sa badhyate
en: Actions do not stain me, and I do not long for their fruit. Whoever knows me in this way is not bound by actions.

sa: एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः।
कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम् ॥
tr: evaṃ jñātvā kṛtaṃ karma pūrvairapi mumukṣubhiḥ
kuru karmaiva tasmāttvaṃ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam
en: Knowing this, the seekers of freedom of old also acted. So you too should act, as the ancients did long ago.
What is action? What is inaction? Even the wise are confused here. I will explain action to you; knowing it, you will be freed from harm.

sa: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः।
tr: karmaṇo hyapi boddhavyaṃ boddhavyaṃ ca vikarmaṇaḥ
en: One must understand action, understand wrong action, and understand inaction. Deep and hard to grasp is the way of action.

sa: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः।
स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥
tr: karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyedakarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ
sa buddhimān manuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt
en: Whoever sees inaction in action and action in inaction is wise among people; that one is a yogi, doing all that is to be done.
One whose every undertaking is free from desire and selfish intent, whose actions are burned in the fire of knowledge, the wise call learned.
Having given up attachment to the fruit of action, always content and dependent on nothing, such a person, though fully engaged in action, does nothing at all.
Expecting nothing, with mind and body under control, letting go of all possessiveness and doing only the work of the body, one incurs no wrong.

sa: समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥
tr: samaḥ siddhāvasiddhau ca kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate
en: Content with whatever comes unasked, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, even in success and failure, such a person acts and is not bound.
For one free from attachment, liberated, whose mind is anchored in knowledge, who works as an offering, all action melts away entirely.
The offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, poured by Brahman into the fire that is Brahman. Brahman alone is reached by one who sees Brahman in every action.
Some yogis offer sacrifice to the gods alone; others offer the sacrifice itself as an oblation into the fire of Brahman.
Some offer hearing and the other senses into the fires of restraint; others offer sound and the other objects of sense into the fires of the senses.
Others offer all the workings of the senses and of the breath into the fire of self-control, kindled by knowledge.
Some offer wealth, some austerity, some yoga; and others, ascetics of firm vows, offer study of scripture and knowledge.
Others, devoted to breath control, offer the in-breath into the out-breath and the out-breath into the in-breath, restraining the flow of both.
Still others, regulating their food, offer the life-breaths into the life-breaths. All of them know sacrifice, and through sacrifice their impurities are destroyed.
Those who eat the nectar left from sacrifice reach the eternal Brahman. This world is not for one who makes no sacrifice; how then the next, best of the Kurus?

sa: एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे।
tr: evaṃ bahuvidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe
en: So many kinds of sacrifice are spread out before Brahman. Know them all as born of action; knowing this, you will be set free.
Better than any sacrifice of material things is the sacrifice of knowledge, scorcher of foes. All action, Partha, finds its completion in knowledge.
Learn it by bowing down, by asking questions and by serving. The wise who have seen the truth will teach you this knowledge.
Knowing it, you will never again fall into delusion like this, Pandava. Through it you will see all beings in your Self, and then in me.
Even if you were the worst of all wrongdoers, you would cross over every wrong by the boat of knowledge alone.
As a blazing fire turns firewood to ashes, Arjuna, so the fire of knowledge turns all actions to ashes.

sa: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते।
tr: na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitramiha vidyate
en: Nothing in this world purifies like knowledge. One perfected in yoga finds it, in time, within oneself.
One with faith, devoted to it, with the senses mastered, gains knowledge; and having gained it, quickly reaches supreme peace.

sa: नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥
tr: nāyaṃ loko'sti na paro na sukhaṃ saṃśayātmanaḥ
en: But the ignorant, the faithless and the doubting perish. For one who doubts, there is neither this world nor the next, nor any happiness.
Actions do not bind one who has renounced action through yoga, whose doubts are cut away by knowledge and who is established in the Self, Dhananjaya.
So, with the sword of knowledge, cut away this doubt born of ignorance that sits in your heart. Take refuge in yoga. Stand up, Bharata!
